title: Two Yeses to Grow, One Veto

scenes.tts: How does a cell decide it can afford to grow? Growth is expensive. Making protein uses amino acids and much of a cell's A T P. So a kinase called M-TOR, inside a complex named M-TOR C one, asks two questions. In the standard model, it switches on only when both get a yes.
scenes.visual: Cell-sized puzzle: a greyed protein synthesis box with a question mark; amino acid and ATP chips are spent into it; the mTORC1 chip appears with two question boxes feeding it; both flip to yes and it lights.
scenes.caption: How does a cell decide it can afford to grow? Growth is expensive. Making protein uses amino acids and much of a cell's ATP. So a kinase called mTOR, inside a complex named mTORC1, asks two questions. In the standard model, it switches on only when both get a yes.
scenes.narration: How does a cell decide it can afford to grow? Growth is expensive. Making protein uses amino acids and much of a cell's ATP. So a kinase called mTOR, inside a complex named mTORC1, asks two questions. In the standard model, it switches on only when both get a yes.

scenes.tts: The first question: has the body said grow? A growth factor switches on Akt. Akt phosphorylates a protein of the T S C complex, which takes the complex out of action. The T S C complex is a GAP, an off switch for a small G T Pase called Rheb. So Rheb stays loaded with G T P. Rheb with G T P is the direct activator of M-TOR C one.
scenes.visual: Growth factor, Akt and TSC chips stack on the right above a membrane bar; a phosphate moves from Akt to TSC, which dims; its bar to Rheb is blocked and a GTP badge flies onto Rheb; mTORC1 appears in the cytoplasm.
scenes.caption: The first question: has the body said grow? A growth factor switches on Akt. Akt phosphorylates a protein of the TSC complex, which takes the complex out of action. The TSC complex is a GAP, an off switch for a small GTPase called Rheb. So Rheb stays loaded with GTP. Rheb with GTP is the direct activator of mTORC1.
scenes.narration: The first question: has the body said grow? A growth factor switches on Akt. Akt phosphorylates a protein of the TSC complex, which takes the complex out of action. The TSC complex is a GAP, an off switch for a small GTPase called Rheb. So Rheb stays loaded with GTP. Rheb with GTP is the direct activator of mTORC1.

scenes.tts: The second question: are there amino acids? How cells sense amino acids was unknown. The link was the Rags, small G T Pases. They do not raise the kinase activity of M-TOR C one. They move it. Without amino acids, M-TOR C one stays spread through the cytoplasm. With them, it gathers on the surface of the lysosome, the cell's acidic digestive compartment. That surface is where it is thought to meet Rheb.
scenes.visual: A dashed receptor box is crossed out and the Rags appear on the membrane; a more-activity arrow on mTORC1 is crossed out; amino acids reach the Rags, which turn on and carry mTORC1 to the membrane next to Rheb.
scenes.caption: The second question: are there amino acids? How cells sense amino acids was unknown. The link was the Rags, small GTPases. They do not raise the kinase activity of mTORC1. That surface is where it is thought to meet Rheb.

scenes.tts: Rheb with G T P can activate only a complex that has been brought to it. Growth factors set whether Rheb is on. Amino acids set delivery, and losing them also calls T S C to Rheb. This is an AND gate. With both, M-TOR C one acts on proteins that control the first step of making protein. With no growth factor, Rheb is off, so the complex stays off. With no amino acids, the complex leaves the lysosome and stays off.
scenes.visual: Two input rows appear and join at an AND badge; with both yes, mTORC1 lights and protein synthesis starts. Case two clears the result and flips growth factor to no: Rheb loses GTP, mTORC1 stays off. Case three clears it again: amino acids no, mTORC1 leaves the membrane, off.

scenes.tts: A third gauge reads energy. A healthy cell keeps A T P nearly constant, so A T P is a poor alarm. A M P moves most. With round numbers, when A T P falls by a tenth, A M P rises almost fourfold. So the kinase A M P K reads A M P. Once on, A M P K makes the T S C complex more active. That drains Rheb of G T P. It also phosphorylates Raptor, which inhibits M-TOR C one. Energy can veto growth, even when growth factors and amino acids are present.
scenes.visual: Bars computed from the adenylate kinase equation: ATP dips a tenth while AMP rises almost fourfold; AMPK appears. Then the fed, lit stage returns: AMPK activates TSC, which drains Rheb, and blocks Raptor; mTORC1 goes dark while growth factor and amino acids stay present.
scenes.caption: A third gauge reads energy. A healthy cell keeps ATP nearly constant, so ATP is a poor alarm. AMP moves most. With round numbers, when ATP falls by a tenth, AMP rises almost fourfold. So the kinase AMPK reads AMP. Once on, AMPK makes the TSC complex more active. That drains Rheb of GTP. It also phosphorylates Raptor, which inhibits mTORC1. Energy can veto growth, even when growth factors and amino acids are present.

scenes.tts: You can now predict a cell. When fed, every input says yes, and protein synthesis runs. With no amino acids, M-TOR C one leaves the lysosome, and translation slows. With no energy, A M P K switches on. It shuts M-TOR C one off, even when everything else is present. Keep this rule: two yeses to grow, and low energy can veto them.
scenes.visual: Three panels built one at a time: fed (all inputs yes, mTORC1 on), no amino acids (off), no energy (a veto bar, off); then the rule line.
